entities.summary: Ehremar or Ebramar or Evremar was a Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem from 1102 to 1105 or 1107, and then Archbishop of Caesarea. Born in Thérouanne, Ponthieu, France around 1100, he was of Frankish noble descent. His tenure as Patriarch was marked by the establishment of the Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem in 1102, which aimed to promote Christian influence in the region. Ebremaro di Thérouanne played a crucial role in the First Crusade, participating in the Siege of Antioch in 1097-1098. He was succeeded by Anselm of Havelock as Patriarch of Jerusalem in 1105. Ebremaro di Thérouanne also served as Archbishop of Caesarea, where he oversaw the construction of several churches and monasteries. His legacy as a prominent figure in the Latin Patriarchate of Jerusalem has endured, with his name becoming synonymous with the institution. Despite his significant contributions to the region, Ebremaro di Thérouanne's life and legacy are not as well-documented as those of his contemporaries, leaving room for further historical investigation.
